title: Ansel and the Ghost
premise: Mirabel Nystrom, a fixer for the Meridian Group — an embassy that exists on no map and answers to no flag — is summoned by a burner phone that rings with the voice of his dead mentor, Ansel. The voice demands he extract a defector carrying proof that the Group's founding families, including Mirabel's own, laundered a massacre into an inheritance. As Mirabel runs the defector across three borders, he discovers the voice is real: Ansel faked his death to test whether his protégé would burn the institution or protect it. In the end, Mirabel chooses neither — he leaks everything, dismantles both the Group and Ansel's design, and finally sleeps through the night.
about_author: Oscar Blackwood is the pen name of a former intelligence contractor who spent eleven years in logistics for organizations he still cannot name. He writes thrillers from a farmhouse in the Baltics, where he claims the nights are quiet enough to hear himself think.

chapters.title: The Phone That Shouldn't Ring
chapters.summary: Mirabel Nystrom, insomnia-wrecked after a botched extraction a year ago, receives a call on a burner buried in his desk drawer. The voice is unmistakably Ansel Voss, his mentor who died twelve months ago. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: dread cracking open into impossible hope.

chapters.title: Meridian House Rules
chapters.summary: Mirabel reports nothing and instead audits the Group's archives, finding Ansel's death certificate signed in his own hand. His handler, Ilsa Brandt, watches him too closely. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: paranoia tightening as loyalty and suspicion blur.

chapters.title: The Defector in Riga
chapters.summary: Ansel's voice gives coordinates: a defector named Katrin Oja holds documents implicating the Group's founding families. Mirabel flies to Riga under a trade cover, sensing a trap but unable to stop. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: fatalistic momentum.

chapters.title: Katrin
chapters.summary: Katrin Oja is sharp, terrified, and carries a ledger of payments routing massacre reparations into private trusts — one trust bearing Mirabel's family name. She doesn't trust him; she's using him as her way out. POV: Katrin. Emotional beat: wary alliance forged from mutual leverage.

chapters.title: First Tail
chapters.summary: Leaving Riga, they spot surveillance — professionals, not police. Mirabel burns a safehouse and reroutes them toward Tallinn while feeding false telemetry to Meridian dispatch. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: the old competence returning like a fever breaking.

chapters.title: What Ansel Taught Me
chapters.summary: A flashback chapter: young Mirabel learning tradecraft and moral arithmetic from Ansel, who insisted justice was a debt institutions could never pay. POV: Mirabel (past). Emotional beat: tenderness shadowed by retrospective doubt about who Ansel really was.

chapters.title: Ilsa's Offer
chapters.summary: Brandt intercepts them at a ferry terminal — not with guns, but with an offer: deliver Katrin, and Mirabel's family's name is scrubbed from the ledger. He pretends to consider. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: temptation wearing a familiar face.

chapters.title: Night Train to Warsaw
chapters.summary: On the night train, Katrin reveals she worked for Ansel before his death — and that he told her to contact Mirabel only if he didn't survive. The phone rings mid-conversation; Ansel hears everything. POV: Katrin. Emotional beat: intimacy built on shared deception.

chapters.title: Warsaw Safehouse
chapters.summary: Holed up in a decommissioned church safehouse, they decrypt part of the ledger: the 'incident' that broke Mirabel's sleep was engineered to bury a witness. His guilt was manufactured. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: grief curdling into rage.

chapters.title: The Second Voice
chapters.summary: The burner calls again — but this time it isn't Ansel. A stranger claims to be the real architect, and says the man on the phone is bait designed to flush out the ledger. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: vertigo; every certainty inverted.

chapters.title: Betrayal Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Mirabel tests both voices against details only the true Ansel would know. One answer fits perfectly — and it means Ansel has been playing him since the funeral. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: cold clarity arriving like a blade.

chapters.title: Border Crossing
chapters.summary: Chased through the Bieszczady mountains, Katrin is wounded covering their escape. Mirabel carries her over the Slovak border, burning his last clean identity. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: devotion hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Founding Families
chapters.summary: In Bratislava, a retired Group archivist confirms the inheritance scheme: four families, four massacres, four generations of quiet profit. Mirabel's grandfather signed the first page. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: inheritance revealed as original sin.

chapters.title: Vienna Dead Drop
chapters.summary: Following Ansel's instructions leads to a Vienna drop containing not documents but a key and an address — Ansel's own apartment, preserved exactly as he left it. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: stepping inside a ghost's life.

chapters.title: Ansel's Apartment
chapters.summary: The apartment holds recordings: Ansel planned everything, including his own death, to force Mirabel to choose between the institution and the truth. The final tape is addressed to him personally. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: betrayal and love indistinguishable.

chapters.title: Ilsa Closes the Net
chapters.summary: Brandt's teams box them in; Katrin is taken. Brandt tells Mirabel plainly: the Group will survive this, and so will he, if he lets it. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: despair at the machine's indifference.

chapters.title: The Exchange
chapters.summary: Ansel's voice proposes a trade: himself, alive and in custody, for Katrin and the ledger. Mirabel realizes Ansel wants to be captured — martyrdom as the final lesson. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: refusal to be anyone's instrument anymore.

chapters.title: Meridian House
chapters.summary: Mirabel walks into headquarters voluntarily, carrying the ledger, and confronts the board — including the second voice, the Group's actual founder. He offers them a choice: publish or perish. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: the fixer fixing the unfixable.

chapters.title: What the Ghost Wanted
chapters.summary: Ansel appears in person — alive, aged, unrepentant. Their confrontation strips the mentor myth bare: Ansel confesses he needed Mirabel to do what he couldn't. Mirabel declines the inheritance of his method. POV: dual. Emotional beat: mourning a living man.

chapters.title: Detonation
chapters.summary: The leak goes out simultaneously through nine channels; the founder's faction moves to erase everyone, but Brandt defects with the internal evidence, tipping the balance. The Group eats itself. Climax: gunfire in the archive vaults. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: chaos as liberation.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Katrin testifies before a tribunal no one expected to matter; the trusts are frozen; Mirabel's name is public and ruined and free. Ansel vanishes, leaving only the burner phone. POV: Katrin. Emotional beat: exhausted, unsentimental hope.

chapters.title: Sleep
chapters.summary: One year later, Mirabel lives quietly under his own name, doing restitution work. The burner rings once; he lets it ring out, then drops it in the sea. That night, he sleeps until morning. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: peace earned, not granted.
